name: str_ilike
title: Detect a pattern the way SQL ILIKE does

origin.description: Match the whole string the way SQL ILIKE does. The wildcards are the same as str_like, and case is ignored.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: Input vector. Either a character vector, or something coercible to one.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: A character vector of SQL LIKE patterns. A stringr modifier is an error. _ matches one character and % matches any number of characters.

origin.details: The pattern is rewritten with the same rules as str_like and then matched as a case-insensitive regular expression. A missing pattern becomes the letters NA inside the anchors. A missing string stays missing.
origin.value: A logical vector the same length as string and pattern.
origin.example:
fruit <- c("apple", "banana", "pear", "pineapple")
result <- str_ilike(fruit, "APP%")
writeLines(paste0('str_ilike(c("apple", "banana", "pear", "pineapple"), "APP%") returns ', paste(result, collapse = ", "), '.'))

translation.description: Match the whole string the way SQL ILIKE does. Case is ignored.

arguments.name: string
arguments.text: A string, stringi._na.NA, or a list of those. A list may carry names.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: A plain string or list of SQL LIKE patterns. A Pattern is rejected with cli_abort.

translation.details: The LIKE text is anchored by like_to_regex, then passed through regex(ignore_case=True) and stri_detect_regex. That is the case-insensitive counterpart of str_like. A modifier is not a LIKE pattern.
translation.value: A list of bools. A missing result is NA.
translation.example:
from stringr.detect import str_ilike
fruit = ["apple", "banana", "pear", "pineapple"]
result = str_ilike(fruit, "APP%")
words = ", ".join("TRUE" if item else "FALSE" for item in result)
print('str_ilike(c("apple", "banana", "pear", "pineapple"), "APP%") returns ' + words + '.')
